key.name: workspace-numbers
key.summary: Number the workspace indicator
key.description: Replace the top bar's workspace dots with numbers that can be clicked to switch, and let Super+1…0 reach a workspace that does not exist yet by creating it.

key.name: autohide
key.summary: Auto-hide the top bar
key.description: Hide the top bar while a window overlaps it, and reveal it when the pointer pushes against the top edge of the screen.

key.name: auto-tile
key.summary: Tile windows as they open
key.description: Give the first window on a workspace the whole of it, and split the focused window to make room for each one after that. Minimize and maximize lose their title bar buttons and their shortcuts while it is on, and get them back when it is switched off; a tiled window that maximizes anyway floats above the others until it is unmaximized, and then takes its tile back.

key.name: float-apps
key.summary: Apps that open floating
key.description: Windows of these apps open floating instead of tiled, in front of the layout. Each entry is an app ID — the name of its .desktop file without the extension, or the window's app ID — matched ignoring case; an entry ending in * matches every ID starting with the rest. The float key still moves a window into the layout or out of it.

key.name: focus-follows-mouse
key.summary: Focus follows the mouse
key.description: Focus the window under the pointer, without raising it, while windows are tiled. GNOME's focus mode is set to sloppy meanwhile, and handed back when this or auto-tiling is switched off.

key.name: debug
key.summary: Log tiling decisions
key.description: Write every layout decision to the journal, for reporting a problem. Off, only errors are logged.

key.name: focus-left
key.summary: Move focus left
key.description: Focus the nearest window left of the focused one. Past the edge of the layout it goes to the monitor that way; it does not wrap around.

key.name: focus-right
key.summary: Move focus right
key.description: Focus the nearest window right of the focused one. Past the edge of the layout it goes to the monitor that way; it does not wrap around.

key.name: focus-up
key.summary: Move focus up
key.description: Focus the nearest window above the focused one. Past the edge of the layout it goes to the monitor that way; it does not wrap around.

key.name: focus-down
key.summary: Move focus down
key.description: Focus the nearest window below the focused one. Past the edge of the layout it goes to the monitor that way; it does not wrap around.

key.name: swap-left
key.summary: Swap with the window left
key.description: Exchange the focused window with the nearest one left of it, leaving the shape of the layout alone; past its edge, with a tiled window on the monitor that way, or into that monitor's layout. Focus follows the window that moved.

key.name: swap-right
key.summary: Swap with the window right
key.description: Exchange the focused window with the nearest one right of it, leaving the shape of the layout alone; past its edge, with a tiled window on the monitor that way, or into that monitor's layout. Focus follows the window that moved.

key.name: swap-up
key.summary: Swap with the window up
key.description: Exchange the focused window with the nearest one above it, leaving the shape of the layout alone; past its edge, with a tiled window on the monitor that way, or into that monitor's layout. Focus follows the window that moved.

key.name: swap-down
key.summary: Swap with the window down
key.description: Exchange the focused window with the nearest one below it, leaving the shape of the layout alone; past its edge, with a tiled window on the monitor that way, or into that monitor's layout. Focus follows the window that moved.

key.name: toggle-float
key.summary: Float the focused window
key.description: Take the focused window out of the tiled layout, restoring the size it had before it was tiled, or put it back in. The rest of the layout closes over the space it leaves.

key.name: toggle-maximize
key.summary: Maximize the focused window
key.description: Maximize the focused window over the layout, or put it back. A maximized tiled window floats above the others and keeps its tile, which it takes back when it is unmaximized.

key.name: toggle-split
key.summary: Flip the split the window sits in
key.description: Turn the division holding the focused window from side by side into stacked, or back.

key.name: toggle-pseudo
key.summary: Pseudo-tile the focused window
key.description: Keep the focused window at the size it had before it was tiled, centred in its share of the layout and scaled down to fit if the share is smaller. Again gives it the whole share back.

key.name: toggle-pop
key.summary: Pop the focused window out
key.description: Lift the focused window out of the layout at 1300×900, centred, in front of every other window and on every workspace. Again puts it back into the layout.

key.name: scratchpad
key.summary: Show or hide the scratchpad
key.description: Bring the windows put away in the scratchpad over the current workspace, or put them away again. Switching workspace puts them away too.

key.name: to-scratchpad
key.summary: Put the focused window in the scratchpad
key.description: Take the focused window out of the layout and put it away in the scratchpad. Floating it back in with the float key returns it to the layout.

key.name: resize-left
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window left
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 100 pixels left, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 100 pixels narrower instead.

key.name: resize-right
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window right
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 100 pixels right, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 100 pixels wider instead.

key.name: resize-up
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window up
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 100 pixels up, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 100 pixels shorter instead.

key.name: resize-down
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window down
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 100 pixels down, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 100 pixels taller instead.

key.name: resize-left-little
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window left a little
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 25 pixels left, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 25 pixels narrower instead.

key.name: resize-right-little
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window right a little
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 25 pixels right, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 25 pixels wider instead.

key.name: resize-up-little
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window up a little
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 25 pixels up, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 25 pixels shorter instead.

key.name: resize-down-little
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window down a little
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 25 pixels down, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 25 pixels taller instead.

key.name: resize-left-lot
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window left a lot
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 300 pixels left, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 300 pixels narrower instead.

key.name: resize-right-lot
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window right a lot
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 300 pixels right, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 300 pixels wider instead.

key.name: resize-up-lot
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window up a lot
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 300 pixels up, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 300 pixels shorter instead.

key.name: resize-down-lot
key.summary: Move the edge beside the focused window down a lot
key.description: Move the nearest division beside the focused window 300 pixels down, growing the window on one side of it and shrinking the one on the other, whichever side the focused window is on. A floating window is made 300 pixels taller instead.

key.name: grow
key.summary: Retired: grow the focused window
key.description: No longer used. Replaced by the resize shortcuts.

key.name: shrink
key.summary: Retired: shrink the focused window
key.description: No longer used. Replaced by the resize shortcuts.

key.name: gap
key.summary: Space between tiled windows
key.description: Space left between neighbouring windows, multiplied by the monitor's scale factor. The layout as a whole sits flush with the screen, apart from the sliver each edge keeps back so that the focused window's outline has somewhere to be drawn.

key.name: border
key.summary: Focused window outline
key.description: Logical pixels of outline drawn around the focused window, and the room kept for it at the edge of the screen, since it is drawn outside the window rather than inside. Zero leaves the layout flush and draws nothing. A window with the workspace to itself is left flush and unmarked either way, since there is nothing to tell it apart from. Drawn in the accent colour; the outline of Ubuntu Tiling Assistant's focus hint is switched off meanwhile.
